proposals.before: He was made consultant on the staff of the right army and marshal of the cloud-banner staff of Prince Yun of Yuzhang, leading his troops to help defend Stone City.
proposals.after: He was made consultant on the staff of the right army and marshal of the Cloud-Banner headquarters of the Prince of Yuzhang, leading his troops to help defend Stone City.
proposals.reason: Chinese 豫章王雲麾府司馬 is the Sima of the Yunhui (Cloud-Banner) headquarters of the Prince of Yuzhang; 雲麾 is an office/title, not the prince's personal name Yun.

proposals.before: He was transferred to Consultant of the Right Army and Marshal of the Cloud-Banner staff of Prince Yun of Yuzhang, leading his troops to help garrison Stone City.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Consultant of the Right Army and Marshal of the Cloud-Banner headquarters of the Prince of Yuzhang, leading his troops to help garrison Stone City.
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 雲麾府 is the Cloud-Banner office, not evidence that the prince was named Yun.

proposals.before: When Runan in Wei submitted, Zhigao was ordered to receive the surrender and was granted acting credentials, made general of swift valor, and appointed regional inspector of Ying province.
proposals.after: When Ruyin in Wei submitted, Zhigao was ordered to receive the surrender and was granted acting credentials, made general of swift valor, and appointed regional inspector of Yingzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 汝陰 is Ruyin, not Runan (汝南); 潁州 is Yingzhou.

proposals.before: When Wei Yin of Runan came over to submit, he was ordered to receive him and was given Acting Credentials, made General of Swift Valor, and Administrator of Ying Province.
proposals.after: When Wei's Ruyin came over to submit, he was ordered to receive it and was given Acting Credentials, made General of Swift Valor, and Regional Inspector of Yingzhou.
proposals.reason: Literal invents personal name 'Wei Yin of Runan'; source is place 汝陰 under Wei submitting.
諡 denotes a posthumous name, not a temple name.

proposals.before: He died; his temple name was Zhuang.
proposals.after: He died; his posthumous name was Zhuang.
proposals.reason: 諡 denotes a posthumous name, not a temple name.

proposals.before: At that time Prince Xunyang Wang Daxin held Jiangzhou; Mei Silì, a deputy of Prince Fan, secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng, but Zhiheng executed Silì and resisted Daxin.
proposals.after: At that time Prince Xunyang Xiao Daxin held Jiangzhou; Mei Sili, a deputy of Prince Fan, secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng, but Zhiheng executed Sili and resisted Daxin.
proposals.reason: Remove odd accent on Sili; 尋陽王大心 is Xiao Daxin, Prince of Xunyang — English 'Wang Daxin' wrongly treats 王 as surname.

proposals.before: Dan had two sons: Yi and Sun.
proposals.after: Dan had two sons: Yi (誼) and Sun (損).
proposals.reason: English Yi/Sun obscure the Chinese given names 誼 and 損; keep names aligned to characters.

proposals.before: His clansman Xiahou Yi served as interior minister of Hengyang; on the day of his farewell audience Dan attended at the imperial seat, and Emperor Wu said to Dan, "Is Xiahou Yi closely related to you or distant?"
proposals.after: His clansman Xiahou Yi (夏侯溢) served as interior minister of Hengyang; on the day of his farewell audience Dan attended at the imperial seat, and Emperor Wu said to Dan, "Is Xiahou Yi closely related to you or distant?"
proposals.reason: Chinese is 夏侯溢; English Yi collides with son 誼's English Yi.

decisions.reason: The phrase 豫章王雲麾府司馬 attaches 雲麾 to the headquarters, not to a personal name. Removing Prince Yun repairs an invented name; the replacement accurately retains the two appointments and defense of Stone City.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷右軍諮議參軍、豫章王雲麾府司馬，率所領助守石頭。

decisions.reason: 豫章王 is the Prince of Yuzhang; 雲麾府 is the Cloud-Banner headquarters. The literal field repeats the same invented Yun name and needs this paired correction. The other Cloud-Banner appointments in this chapter corroborate the office reading.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遷右軍諮議參軍、豫章王雲麾府司馬，率所領助守石頭。

decisions.after: When Ruyin in Wei submitted, Zhigao was ordered to receive the surrender and was granted acting credentials, made general of swift valor, and appointed regional inspector of Ying province.
decisions.reason: 汝陰 is Ruyin, not 汝南 (Runan). Retain the already accurate Ying province for 潁州: changing that to Yingzhou is unnecessary romanization, not a fidelity repair. The idiomatic field already correctly identifies the provincial office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時魏汝陰來附，敕之高應接，仍除假節、飆勇將軍、潁州刺史。

decisions.after: When Ruyin in Wei came over to submit, he was ordered to receive the surrender and was given Acting Credentials, made General of Swift Valor, and Regional Inspector of Ying Province.
decisions.reason: 時魏汝陰來附 names a Wei locality submitting, not a man named Wei Yin of Runan. Receive the surrender removes the invented personal recipient without the awkward receive it. 刺史 is the regional inspector, not the commandery administrator; retain Ying Province.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時魏汝陰來附，敕之高應接，仍除假節、飆勇將軍、潁州刺史。

decisions.reason: 諡曰烈 gives a posthumous name, Lie, not a temple name. The idiomatic field already has the correct distinction. This decision changes no dates or extracted posthumous-name claims.
卒，諡曰壯 reports death and the posthumous name Zhuang. Nothing denotes a temple name. The idiomatic field is already correct, and the source supplies no calendar date here.

decisions.after: At that time Daxin, Prince of Xunyang, held Jiangzhou; Mei Sili, a deputy of Prince Fan, secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng, but Zhiheng executed Sili and resisted Daxin.
decisions.reason: 尋陽王大心 means Daxin, Prince of Xunyang: 王 is the rank, not the surname Wang, and Xunyang is the title locality. Use the source-given Daxin without adding Xiao. Retain the actions and existing place rendering. The unaccented Sili is acceptable but does not invalidate the extracted accented alias.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時尋陽王大心在江州，範副梅思立密要大心襲湓城，之橫斬思立而拒大心。

decisions.reason: 亶二子：誼，損 is already accurately rendered as Dan having two sons, Yi and Sun. The proposal merely adds Chinese characters to finished English. The next two units distinguish the sons by context; structured claims retain their Chinese names.

夏侯溢 is already correctly romanized Xiahou Yi. Adding Chinese characters does not repair a mistranslation. The clan relationship dialogue in s0155-s0157 distinguishes this man from Dan's sons in s0164-s0166; shared romanization is not evidence of shared identity.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宗人夏侯溢爲衡陽內史，辭日，亶侍御坐，高祖謂亶曰：「夏侯溢於卿疏近？」

proposals.reason: 諡曰恭 gives the posthumous name Gong, not a temple name. The idiomatic field already makes the correct distinction.

proposals.before: At that time Prince Xunyang Wang Daxin was in Jiangzhou; Fan's deputy Mei Silì secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng; Zhiheng beheaded Silì and resisted Daxin.
proposals.after: At that time Daxin, Prince of Xunyang, was in Jiangzhou; Fan's deputy Mei Sili secretly urged Daxin to attack Pencheng; Zhiheng beheaded Sili and resisted Daxin.
proposals.reason: Paired-field correction for r0007: 尋陽王大心 names Daxin, Prince of Xunyang, not Wang Daxin. Preserve the literal actions; no inferred surname or Chinese annotation is needed.

proposals.after: Posthumously he was honored as Palace Attendant and Duke of Works; his posthumous name was Zhongzhuang.
proposals.reason: 諡曰忠壯 gives the posthumous name Zhongzhuang. Correct the repeated temple-name error while leaving the other offices outside this narrow proposal unchanged.
諡曰襄 gives the posthumous name Xiang, not a temple name. The idiomatic field is already correct.
諡曰桓 gives the posthumous name Huan, not a temple name. The idiomatic field is already correct.

proposals.reason: 諡曰宜侯 gives a posthumous title: 宜 is Yi and 侯 is the rank Marquis, not part of a personal name Yihou. Correct both the temple-name category and the untranslated rank.

proposals.after: His posthumous title was Marquis Yi.
proposals.reason: The paired idiomatic field also leaves 侯 untranslated inside Yihou. Render the rank in the posthumous title 宜侯 as Marquis Yi; do not infer a temple name or a date.

decisions.reason: The source explicitly says 諡曰恭. 諡 is a posthumous name, not a temple name; Gong is already correctly rendered in the idiomatic field. The proposed single category correction is supported.

In 時尋陽王大心在江州, 尋陽王 is Daxin's princely title, not the personal surname Wang. The proposed literal rendering matches this syntax and the independently corrected idiomatic field, while preserving the subsequent agents and actions. Mei Sili is the unaccented rendering of 梅思立.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 時尋陽王大心在江州，範副梅思立密要大心襲湓城，之橫斬思立而拒大心。

decisions.reason: 贈侍中、司空公，諡曰忠壯 distinguishes posthumous offices from the posthumous name Zhongzhuang. Replacing temple name with posthumous name corrects the category without changing the rest of this sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贈侍中、司空公，諡曰忠壯。

decisions.reason: 諡曰襄 explicitly gives the posthumous name Xiang. No temple name is asserted; the proposed literal correction agrees with the Chinese and the already correct idiomatic field.
諡曰桓 explicitly gives the posthumous name Huan. The source supplies no temple name; correcting that noun phrase is warranted while preserving the given Romanization.

In 諡曰宜侯, 宜 supplies the posthumous epithet Yi and 侯 is the rank marquis. Marquis Yi translates that rank rather than fusing it into Yihou, and posthumous title avoids the false temple-name category. Both English fields need the same correction.
